editorial.title: 진흙탕 싸움만 하다 끝나는 민주당 대표 경선
editorial.body: (사설) 더불어민주당 당대표 선거가 네거티브와 계파 갈등으로 치열하게 펼쳐지며 정책·비전 경쟁은 실종됐다. 집권당 대표는 국정 운영과 당내 통합, 민심 회복이 중요하나, 이번 경선에서는 진흙탕 싸움과 투표율 저하, 분열 우려가 커지고 있다. |

정책과 비전 논쟁은 사라지고 진흙탕 싸움만 벌어진다.
투표율 저하와 당내 분열 우려가 커지고 있다.
editorial.pullQuote: 집권당 대표는 국정 운영과 당내 통합, 민심 회복이 중요하나 진흙탕 싸움만 펼쳐진다.
editorial.stance: 집권당의 책임감 있는 리더십 경쟁이 아닌 진흙탕 싸움은 국민 신뢰를 잃게 할 것이다.
editorial.titleTr: Democratic Party Leadership Race Devolves Into Mud-Slinging Match
summaryTr: The Democratic Party leadership race has been marked by negative campaigning and factional conflict.
Policy and vision debates have disappeared, leaving only mudslinging.
Concerns are growing over declining voter turnout and internal party division.

The ruling party's leader must prioritize state governance, internal party unity, and winning back public trust, yet this primary is marked by mudslinging, declining voter turnout, and growing concerns over party division.

editorial.body: 청와대와 여권이 추진하는 4년 중임 대통령제 개헌 논의를 분석함. 현직 대통령의 연임을 금지한 헌법 정신을 강조하며, 개헌의 순수성을 입증하기 위해 대통령이 직접 연임 포기를 선언해야 개헌 동력을 얻을 수 있음을 주장함.

editorial.titleTr: Opinion: If You Really Want Constitutional Reform, First Declare You Won't Seek Reelection
summaryTr: The purity of the constitutional amendment for a four-year single term being pursued by the presidential office is being called into question.
The prohibition on consecutive reelection of the sitting president is a core principle of the constitution.
A presidential declaration renouncing reelection must precede securing momentum for constitutional reform.
editorial.bodyTr: An analysis of the constitutional amendment discussions regarding a four-year, single-term presidential system being pursued by the Blue House and the ruling party. The editorial emphasizes the constitutional spirit that prohibits a sitting president from seeking reelection, arguing that in order to gain momentum for the constitutional amendment, the president must personally declare a renunciation of reelection to prove the purity of the amendment initiative.

editorial.titleTr: Editorial: Water Resource Strategy Becomes Urgent Priority as Severe Droughts Become the New Normal
summaryTr: As extreme droughts become commonplace, 200 fire trucks have been deployed nationwide and water rationing measures are being implemented.
Existing reservoirs at 99.6% capacity are only prepared for once-in-a-decade droughts, leaving them vulnerable to extreme droughts occurring once every 20 years.
Water management policies have been inconsistent with each change of administration, and dam construction taking 10 to 20 years results in belated responses.
editorial.bodyTr: About 200 fire trucks from across the nation were recently dispatched to South Gyeongsang Province following a national emergency mobilization order, with military personnel from the Army, Navy, and Air Force also set to be deployed to combat an extreme drought gripping the region. Prolonged dry spells and temperatures exceeding 40 degrees Celsius have caused agricultural reservoirs to dry up and forced water rationing for drinking water. After striking the Yeongdong region last year, Honam in 2022, and Yeongnam this year, climate disasters have become so unpredictable that it is difficult to forecast which region will be hit next year. As climate-related disasters grow more frequent and their damages mount, the nation must now adopt bold and aggressive water management strategies with extreme droughts and floods treated as constants. Above all, expansion of water management infrastructure is urgently needed. In particular, the Gwangju area, where semiconductor megaprojects are being pursued, faces concerns over water shortages and requires extraordinary measures to secure additional water resources. The current Yeongnam drought is occurring at a once-in-20-years frequency, yet 99.6 percent of the 3,422 reservoirs managed nationwide by the Korea Rural Community Corporation were designed to withstand only ordinary droughts occurring at once-in-10-years frequency or less. These facilities must be substantially reinforced to withstand "severe droughts" occurring at intervals of 20 years or longer. Although the United Nations first released an official report warning of the dangers of global warming and climate crisis in 1990, South Korea's response has been slow and inconsistent. In particular, plans to prepare for heat waves, droughts, and floods have wavered according to the ideological orientation of successive administrations. For example, the Lee Myung-bak government prepared a "long-term dam construction plan (2012-2021)" that included 14 candidate dam sites in 2012, but the Moon Jae-in government suspended it in 2018. The Yoon Suk-yeol government promoted the construction of 14 new climate-response dams, but the Lee Jae-myung government canceled 7 of them in September last year. When concerns were raised about securing water supplies for new semiconductor factories in Honam, the government belatedly mentioned reviewing the option of new dam construction, which comes too little, too late. Dam construction is a long-term project that takes 10 to 20 years, including site selection, land compensation, and construction lasting 6 to 7 years. If the government had pursued dam construction as planned back in 2012, the current water shortage crisis could have been mitigated. The government must now abandon environmental fundamentalism and develop practical water management strategies including new dam construction, water supply system improvements, wastewater recycling, seawater desalination, and groundwater utilization.

leanScore.rationale: 환경근본주의 비판, 댐 건설 필요성 강조, 이전 진보 정부의 댐 계획 중단 비판 등 개발-실용주의적 프레임으로 진보 정책을 부정적으로 평가

editorial.title: AI-driven search shift
editorial.body: Google’s rise in Korea illustrates why portals like Naver must adapt to AI era For two decades, opening the internet in South Korea often meant opening Naver. In July, that habit slipped, exposing a deeper change in how Koreans find and consume information. Google’s mobile app recorded 47.02 million monthly active users (MAUs) in Korea, edging past Naver’s 46.85 million, according to Mobile Index. MAU measures whether an app was used at least once during a month, though it says little about time spent or search volume and excludes PC web traffic. Naver still holds more than 60 percent of traditional desktop and direct search traffic, compared with Google’s mid-30s share. The mobile figures therefore do not establish a new market order. They do, however, reveal where user behavior may be heading. Google has added about 8 million Korean mobile users in 18 months, while Naver’s growth has been much slower. Google has also pushed its Gemini AI deeper into search and mobile services. Features such as Circle to Search on Samsung Galaxy smartphones let users reach Google without opening a conventional search page. For years, Korean search revolved around major portals like Naver and Daum. Users entered through a portal site, typed keywords and worked through links, reviews and community posts. Generative AI is changing that routine. People can ask questions in ordinary language and receive synthesized answers, sometimes through images or voice. The search box is becoming an interface rather than a destination. ChatGPT’s growth adds weight to the shift. The AI chatbot developed by OpenAI recorded 16.46 million Korean MAUs in July, about 2.6 times Daum’s 6.31 million. A 2025 government survey found that 60 percent of generative AI users had shifted at least half of their conventional search activity to artificial intelligence. Against this backdrop, Naver faces a technological challenge alongside its market-share problem. Its strength was built on a dense domestic ecosystem of news, user-generated content, reviews and community knowledge. Yet a search environment crowded with sponsored results and promotional content can make useful information harder to find. Naver’s closed ecosystem also looks less compelling when AI systems can draw on the wider web. The consequences extend beyond Naver. Search traffic produces a steady stream of local, original information. If domestic platforms lose users, the supply of high-quality Korean data could shrink, weakening the foundation for locally developed AI. The AI-powered digital shift deserves attention from policymakers since data sovereignty is tied to the continued production and preservation of reliable domestic information, wherever users choose to search. Yet protecting Naver from competition would miss the point. Global tech firms spend tens of billions of dollars annually on computing infrastructure, chips and data centers. Expecting a Korean portal to match hyperscalers in general-purpose AI would be an expensive way to chase a losing game. Policymakers should instead focus on the conditions for competition. Korea needs cheaper access to computing power and energy, clearer rules for AI training and copyright. Regulations should also avoid weighing more heavily on companies simply because they fall within easy domestic jurisdiction. Naver also needs to reconsider where it can win. Its investment in Anthropic points toward cooperation with global AI developers, while its stronger advantage may lie in areas rich in Korean data and local networks. Korean portals should focus on logistics, commerce and other specialized services that offer more defensible opportunities than trying to replicate the largest AI foundation models. The July search numbers may reverse next month. What is harder to reverse is the change in how people look for information. Naver once owned the starting point of the Korean internet. AI is making the starting point much harder to own, while making alternatives easier to reach. summaryTr: 구글의 모바일 앱이 한국 사용자 수에서 네이버를 앞지르면서 AI 기반 검색으로의 전환을 시사했다.
생성형 AI가 자연어 질의와 종합된 답변으로 기존 포털 기반 검색을 대체하고 있다.
네이버는 글로벌 AI 거인들과 경쟁하려는 대신 지역 데이터와 특화 서비스로 경쟁해야 한다.
editorial.bodyTr:
구글의 한국 성장이 보여주는 포털의 과제, AI 시대에 적응해야 한다

지난 20년간 한국에서 인터넷을 켠다는 것은 네이버를 켠다는 의미였다. 7월, 그 습관이 흔들리면서 한국인들이 정보를 찾고 소비하는 방식의 더 근본적인 변화가 드러났다. 모바일 인덱스에 따르면 구글의 모바일 앱이 월 활성 사용자(MAU) 4,702만 명으로 네이버의 4,685만 명을 근소하게 앞질렀다. editorials.title: AI-driven search shift
editorials.body: Google’s rise in Korea illustrates why portals like Naver must adapt to AI era For two decades, opening the internet in South Korea often meant opening Naver. In July, that habit slipped, exposing a deeper change in how Koreans find and consume information. Google’s mobile app recorded 47.02 million monthly active users (MAUs) in Korea, edging past Naver’s 46.85 million, according to Mobile Index. MAU measures whether an app was used at least once during a month, though it says little about time spent or search volume and excludes PC web traffic. Naver still holds more than 60 percent of traditional desktop and direct search traffic, compared with Google’s mid-30s share. The mobile figures therefore do not establish a new market order. They do, however, reveal where user behavior may be heading. Google has added about 8 million Korean mobile users in 18 months, while Naver’s growth has been much slower. Google has also pushed its Gemini AI deeper into search and mobile services. Features such as Circle to Search on Samsung Galaxy smartphones let users reach Google without opening a conventional search page. For years, Korean search revolved around major portals like Naver and Daum. Users entered through a portal site, typed keywords and worked through links, reviews and community posts. Generative AI is changing that routine. People can ask questions in ordinary language and receive synthesized answers, sometimes through images or voice. The search box is becoming an interface rather than a destination. ChatGPT’s growth adds weight to the shift. The AI chatbot developed by OpenAI recorded 16.46 million Korean MAUs in July, about 2.6 times Daum’s 6.31 million. A 2025 government survey found that 60 percent of generative AI users had shifted at least half of their conventional search activity to artificial intelligence. Against this backdrop, Naver faces a technological challenge alongside its market-share problem. Its strength was built on a dense domestic ecosystem of news, user-generated content, reviews and community knowledge. Yet a search environment crowded with sponsored results and promotional content can make useful information harder to find. Naver’s closed ecosystem also looks less compelling when AI systems can draw on the wider web. The consequences extend beyond Naver. Search traffic produces a steady stream of local, original information. If domestic platforms lose users, the supply of high-quality Korean data could shrink, weakening the foundation for locally developed AI. The AI-powered digital shift deserves attention from policymakers since data sovereignty is tied to the continued production and preservation of reliable domestic information, wherever users choose to search. Yet protecting Naver from competition would miss the point. Global tech firms spend tens of billions of dollars annually on computing infrastructure, chips and data centers. Expecting a Korean portal to match hyperscalers in general-purpose AI would be an expensive way to chase a losing game. Policymakers should instead focus on the conditions for competition. Korea needs cheaper access to computing power and energy, clearer rules for AI training and copyright. Regulations should also avoid weighing more heavily on companies simply because they fall within easy domestic jurisdiction. Naver also needs to reconsider where it can win. Its investment in Anthropic points toward cooperation with global AI developers, while its stronger advantage may lie in areas rich in Korean data and local networks. Korean portals should focus on logistics, commerce and other specialized services that offer more defensible opportunities than trying to replicate the largest AI foundation models. The July search numbers may reverse next month. What is harder to reverse is the change in how people look for information. Naver once owned the starting point of the Korean internet. AI is making the starting point much harder to own, while making alternatives easier to reach. summaryTr: Ruling party lawmakers are collectively opposing the government's real estate tax reform plan.
They point to a collapse of trust, citing it as a violation of presidential campaign promises.
The policy's momentum is being significantly shaken by internal opposition within the ruling party.
editorial.bodyTr: Backlash is erupting within the ruling party over the government's real estate tax reform proposal. At a Democratic Party of Korea caucus meeting on the 13th, harsh criticism poured out, including statements like "The president said multiple times he wouldn't use taxes to control housing prices, but that trust has been broken" and "If we go forward like this, we'll face a complete disaster in either the general or presidential election." summary: 산업용 전기료를 권역별로 차등 적용하는 방안이 제시되고 있다.
지역 간 에너지 비용 격차가 기업 경쟁력에 영향을 미친다.
정부는 국가경쟁력 차원에서 전기료 정책을 재검토해야 한다.
editorials.stance: 지역별 전기료 차등화를 통해 산업 경쟁력을 강화할 필요가 있다는 입장
editorials.titleTr: Editorial: Regional Disparities in Industrial Electricity Rates Demand National Competitiveness Approach
summaryTr: Plans are being proposed to apply differential industrial electricity rates by region.
Energy cost disparities between regions affect corporate competitiveness.
The government should review electricity rate policy from a national competitiveness perspective.

leanScore.label: Lean conservative
leanScore.rationale: 기업 경쟁력과 국가경쟁력 차원의 정책 재검토를 강조하며 산업계 입장을 대변하는 시장친화적 프레이밍
